Let’s talk about Chapter 8—Navigating Performance Challenges: Managing Around Weaknesses.
You know, even in the most strengths-focused workplaces, weaknesses and performance bumps are bound to show up. The real trick isn’t to ignore them, or to try and “fix” people. Instead, it’s about recognizing what makes each person valuable, and figuring out how to work around those rough edges.
Think about it: what if, instead of forcing someone to get better at something that just drains them, you changed the game? Maybe you tweak their job a bit, so they spend less time on tasks that don’t play to their strengths. Or you team them up with someone whose skills balance out their weak spots.
Picture this—a brilliant strategist who’s always full of ideas, but maybe isn’t the best at follow-through. Pair them with a teammate who’s detail-oriented and great at execution, and suddenly, the whole team benefits.
Here are a few practical ways to manage around weaknesses:
First, there’s job crafting. That’s just a fancy way of saying: adjust people’s roles so they can do more of what energizes them, and less of what drags them down.
Next, try team pairing. Match folks with complementary strengths so they can cover for each other’s blind spots.
Then there’s skill-sharing. Encourage everyone to teach each other—the team grows together, and those weaknesses can actually turn into new learning moments.
And of course, set clear boundaries. Be honest about what’s unlikely to change, and make sure expectations are realistic.
Here’s something to pay attention to: not every weakness can be managed around. If someone can’t meet the basic requirements of their role, it might be time to consider a different position—or, sometimes, a tough conversation about moving on. The key is to approach it with empathy and clarity, not avoidance.
So, what’s the big takeaway? When you focus on what people do best, and get creative about working around their limitations, everyone gets a chance to shine. You’ll see less frustration, more confidence, and—let’s be honest—better results all around.
